clue.text: Party respecting local boss

parts.note: re means concerning or respecting
a local is a pub, and its boss is the publican, the landlord

explanation.surface: A political party seems to show deference to the man who runs the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' is British slang for one's nearby pub; it looks like it qualifies a council boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A Republican is a member or supporter of a political party, such as the US Republican Party.

clue.text: Swing, an alternative to jazz

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to sway or swing to and fro
second meaning: ... music, another genre of popular music

explanation.walkthrough: Swing is itself a style of jazz, so the clue reads as a musical comparison throughout.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to sway back and forth and the guitar-based music genre distinct from jazz.

clue.text: Drivel Yankee's written about game. Tut having read this before?

parts.note: pap is worthless or trivial talk

indicators.note: the letters for Yankee's are written around the game, enclosing it

parts.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO alphabet, and the possessive adds S
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: Nonsense written about a game by an American, followed by an odd question about a boy king's reading.
explanation.walkthrough: Tut is Tutankhamun, the Egyptian pharaoh; the question asks what he might have read from, long before paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Egyptians wrote on sheets made from the reed, so a pharaoh would have read from that material.

clue.text: Crossing road, help Sheila with babe, unruly kid

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so the letters of the two names are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
to kid is to con, to fool someone

explanation.surface: A woman with her baby and a disobedient child are getting over the street.
explanation.walkthrough: A Belisha beacon is the flashing orange globe on a post at British zebra crossings, named after the minister Leslie Hore-Belisha.
explanation.definitionFit: The beacon marks a pedestrian crossing, so it is an aid for people getting across the street.

clue.text: One Native American moving north, without reservation

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: moving tells us the letter for north shifts its place within the name, here up to the top of the down entry

parts.note: Tonto is the Native American companion of the Lone Ranger
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A Native American heads north, leaving a reservation with no restrictions.
explanation.walkthrough: In TONTO the N moves up to the front, giving NTOTO, after I. 'Reservation' nods at Native American lands, but the definition means 'entirely'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means completely or as a whole, which is agreeing with no qualification held back.

clue.text: Secure site royal lady erected to house large pet?

indicators.note: to house is to contain, so the reversed name holds the other letters
in a down entry, erected means written upwards, so the name is reversed

parts.note: Zara Tindall, the Princess Royal's daughter
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a cat is a typical pet

explanation.surface: A royal lady puts up a secure enclosure for a big pet.
explanation.walkthrough: Zara reversed is ARAZ; placing L and CAT inside gives the prison's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcatraz was the famous maximum-security federal prison on an island in San Francisco Bay.

clue.text: Combatant's heading here in The Colosseum, perhaps, with it

indicators.note: a word's heading is its opening letter, so only the start of the word is used

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken
hic is Latin for here, as might be said in ancient Rome

explanation.surface: A gladiator's leader is here in the Roman arena, along with something.
explanation.walkthrough: The Colosseum stands for Rome and so for Latin, the language spoken there.
explanation.definitionFit: With it is slang for fashionable or stylish, which is what chic means.

clue.text: Henry the Eighth in difficulty maintaining former grip

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so the first letters keep the second within them

parts.note: Hal is a familiar form of Henry, as Shakespeare's Prince Hal
old means former, as in an old flame

indicators.note: this picks the eighth letter of the following word

parts.note: the word whose eighth letter is taken

explanation.surface: King Henry VIII, in trouble, keeps his old power over people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Henry the Eighth' looks like the king, but Henry is HAL and 'the Eighth in difficulty' is its eighth letter, L. HALL holds OLD.
explanation.definitionFit: A grip is an old word for a travelling bag, which is what a holdall is.

clue.text: Keen on parking, to spread upturned treasure hunt, say

parts.note: to keen is to wail or cry in grief
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

indicators.note: in a down entry, upturned means written bottom to top, so the word is reversed

parts.note: marg is short for margarine, a spread

explanation.surface: Someone eager about parking sets out an overturned treasure hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: MARG reversed is GRAM. A treasure hunt is offered as an example of something set out in coded clues.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptogram is a coded puzzle, and a treasure hunt's clues are an example of such a coded message.

clue.text: Zeppelin crewman, say, knocked back sauce with band in resting place

indicators.note: the reversed sauce and the band go inside the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: knocked back means turned back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: lip and sauce both mean cheek or impudence
O is a ring or band by its shape

explanation.surface: An airship crew member drank some sauce with a pop group in his bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Zeppelin suggests both the airship and the rock band Led Zeppelin; an airship's second pilot is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A Zeppelin airship had a second pilot alongside the captain, so such a crewman is an example of the job.

clue.text: Fancy dress business spread

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business
to splay is to spread out

explanation.surface: A costume firm has expanded its operations.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosplay is dressing up as characters from films, games or comics, which is a form of costume wear.

clue.text: Mark on light bag identifying fish

parts.note: a speck is a small mark or spot
an LED is a light-emitting diode, a light
bag and trout are both slang for an unpleasant old woman

explanation.surface: A stain on a lightweight bag lets you tell what fish it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old trout' and 'old bag' are both British insults for a disagreeable woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The speckled trout is a species of fish, also called the brook trout or spotted seatrout.

clue.text: As gull might upset boat, hire site tense

indicators.note: upset means overturned or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A gull could overturn a boat, and the place renting it out gets nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: Gull is both a seabird, which literally rises to bait, and a gullible person, who reacts as provoked.
explanation.definitionFit: A gull is a dupe, someone easily fooled, and the idiom means to react exactly as a provoker intended.

clue.text: Conceal line that's caught species on great oceans etc

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece on another sits above it
caught here means heard, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: conceal is hide and a line is a row, so together hide row
sp is the standard abbreviation for species
ace means excellent or great

explanation.surface: Hide the fishing line that has hooked creatures out on the vast seas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' looks like fishing, but it means heard: HIDE ROW said aloud gives HYDRO.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrospace is the underwater realm of the world's seas, treated as an environment like outer space.

clue.text: One usually going along with right player

parts.note: right! and yes! are both cries of agreement
a man is a player or piece in a board game such as draughts

explanation.surface: Someone who normally sides with the right-wing actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A yes-man is a sycophant who agrees with whatever a superior says, always falling in line.

clue.text: John and Penny pull, coupling

parts.note: Jack is a familiar form of John
to lug is to drag or pull

explanation.surface: John and Penny are attracted to each other and pair up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull' is British slang for attracting a romantic partner, which is how the surface reads.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack plug is an electrical connector, so it is a device for joining a lead to equipment.

clue.text: Having drawn out edges, square yard joiner's cutting causes dilemma

indicators.note: the joining word cuts into the other letters, going inside them
with its edges drawn out, the word keeps only its inner letters

parts.note: the word whose inner letters are kept
and is a joining word, a conjunction, and the possessive is the clue's 's for is

explanation.surface: A carpenter's cut through a squared-off yard of timber leaves a quandary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joiner' looks like a carpenter, but it means a conjunction. QUAR plus Y is QUARY, and AND goes in after QU.
explanation.definitionFit: A quandary is a state of uncertainty over what to do, which is a dilemma.

clue.text: After performing meets resistance, I'm daft reciting poems

indicators.note: after places the word for performing behind the letter for resistance

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for resistance
on means performing, as an actor on stage

indicators.note: reciting means speaking aloud, so the cry is taken by its sound

parts.note: doh is the cry of someone admitting they've been stupid

explanation.surface: Someone forgets their lines while performing poetry and blames their own silliness.
explanation.walkthrough: DOH, as Homer Simpson exclaims, sounds like the French ending DEAUX.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondeau is a short French verse form with a refrain, so the plural names a set of such verses.

clue.text: Fanatical individual in blue, head over heels as Rovers appear

indicators.note: the fanatical individual is put inside the reversed word
head over heels means upside down, so in a down entry the word is reversed

parts.note: blue is the colour of the Conservatives, so a Tory is a Con
mad means fanatical, as in mad about football
I is one, a single individual

explanation.surface: A fan in blue tumbles over as the Rovers football team takes the field.
explanation.walkthrough: Rovers looks like a football club, but here it means wanderers. CON reversed is NOC, holding MADI.
explanation.definitionFit: Rovers are wanderers, and wandering from place to place without a settled home is being nomadic.

clue.text: Angles seen here in mosaic remain reflex

indicators.note: reflex means bent back, so the hidden letters are read backwards
in signals the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: In geometry, reflex angles show up within a tiled design.
explanation.walkthrough: Angles and reflex suggest geometry, but the Angles were the Germanic people who settled England.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercia was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom in the English Midlands, settled by the Germanic Angles.

clue.text: Shell mechanic's last mug seen under vehicle

indicators.note: in a down entry, under places these letters below the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: last picks the final letter of the word

parts.note: the word whose final letter is taken
a mug and an ass are both fools

explanation.surface: A garage mechanic's final idiot is found lying under a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A carcass is the framework or hollow body of something, so it is a shell or skeleton structure.

clue.text: Help key recruits from America cooking certain cuisine

indicators.note: recruits means takes in, so the letters for America go inside

parts.note: F1 is the help key on a computer keyboard, with the 1 read as I
US means American, from the United States
on means cooking, as a dish on the stove

explanation.surface: An American assistant is drafted in to cook a particular style of food.
explanation.definitionFit: Fusion is a style of cooking that blends ingredients and methods from several culinary traditions.

clue.text: Person only qualified to work on single-deckers in part of circuit?

definitions.text: Person only qualified to work on single-deckers in part of circuit?

parts.words: Person only qualified to work on single-deckers in part of circuit?
parts.note: a bus conductor on a single-decker bus would be a half or semi version of one, if a double-decker is the full bus

explanation.walkthrough: A single-decker is half a double-decker, so its conductor is a semi-conductor; the answer is also an electronic component.
explanation.definitionFit: A semiconductor is a material such as silicon used in transistors and chips that form parts of electronic circuitry.

clue.text: Vulgar regulars in already drinking whiskey

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the alternate letters contain the other one
regular letters of a word are every other one, here the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: the word whose alternate letters are taken
Whiskey is W in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: The rude pub regulars have already been drinking whiskey.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewd means crude and indecent, especially in a sexual way, which fits coarse or obscene.

clue.text: Supplements tot with Scotch and soda finally

parts.note: to tot up is to add
to scotch a plan is to put an end to it

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word

parts.note: the word whose final letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone tops up a small drink with Scotch whisky and soda.
explanation.walkthrough: Tot and Scotch and soda read as drinks; tot is ADD, as in tot up, and Scotch is the verb END.
explanation.definitionFit: Addenda are extra items appended to a book or document, so they are additions to it.

clue.text: Period piece central in Thirsk on decline

indicators.note: a piece from the centre of the word, its two middle letters

parts.note: Thirsk is a market town in North Yorkshire; its middle letters are taken
to age is to decline with the years

explanation.surface: A historical costume drama set in the middle of Thirsk is going downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Period piece' looks like a single phrase, but the definition is just 'Period'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iron Age is a prehistoric era when iron tools came into use, following the Bronze Age.

clue.text: Continuing in the same way, Hearts score

parts.note: etc, et cetera, means and so on
H is the card abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: Heart of Midlothian keeps up its form and gets a goal.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearts is a Scottish football club, which is how the surface reads.
explanation.definitionFit: To score a surface is to cut lines into it, and etching is incising a design.

clue.text: Riveted into ground with much puff, outhouse exhausts husband

indicators.note: much of a word is most of it, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: puff is hype, excessive promotion

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: exhausts means uses up or empties out, so the letter for husband goes

parts.note: a shed is an outhouse

explanation.surface: Something hammered into the ground, with heavy breathing, while the shed wears out a husband.
explanation.walkthrough: HYP is most of HYPE; 'ground' rearranges INTO as NOTI; SHED losing H is SED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be hypnotised is to be spellbound or completely captivated, which is to be riveted.
